Mission

Climate adaptation for lives well lived

DigiÉire’s mission is to put wellbeing at the centre of flood adaptation in Ireland. We are developing a digital twin to explore how a changing climate and the decisions made today could shape people’s lives through to 2100, assessing progress beyond GDP and economic losses.

Global warming is melting glaciers and ice sheets, expanding the oceans and intensifying heavy rainfall. Ireland’s position on the Atlantic edge of Europe gives these changes particular significance. Its extensive coastline and communities beside rivers and estuaries are exposed to coastal and inland flooding. Rising seas and heavier downpours can place growing pressure on homes, infrastructure and essential services.

Ireland’s climate is closely tied to the Atlantic. Prevailing winds and ocean currents, including the warm North Atlantic Drift, help maintain its mild maritime climate, while Atlantic weather systems bring wind and rain. Changes in the wider Atlantic circulation, including the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC), could alter this climate further. Their local effects remain uncertain, strengthening the case for adaptation that works across a range of plausible futures. Met Éireann’s climate overview and AMOC assessment explain these influences.

Flooding affects more than property and economic output. Displacement, disruption to daily life and anxiety about future events can affect health, financial security and people’s connection to their community. These consequences are unevenly distributed: people differ in their exposure, resources and capacity to recover. Understanding those differences is essential to fair and effective adaptation.

DigiÉire combines climate and flood scenarios with a dynamic agent-based model of Ireland’s population to examine how risks and adaptation choices could affect wellbeing over time. Our aim is to help identify choices that protect quality of life, reduce inequalities and support communities across generations. This responds to the EPA’s assessment of Ireland’s climate risks, which identifies flooding among the risks requiring adaptation.

How can Ireland adapt to flooding in ways that help people live well, now and through to 2100?

  • Ireland — communities facing coastal and inland flooding
  • To 2100 — exploring long-term risks and adaptation choices
  • Beyond GDP — wellbeing, equity and quality of life
